We Tested Waiting for the 1H and 4H EMAs to Agree

Episode A32 · DESCRIPTIVE; no interval or luck inference

These two index funds, SPY and QQQ; this entry (ours); these costs; 2004-2026 with no QQQ trades from late July 2004 to mid-December 2011. EARLY is mostly SPY. Iliya, on indices: 'But on indices, I use a bit more of a VWAP' (471.12-479.919s).

R PER TRADE = RESULT / PLANNED RISK PER SHARE, fixed before entry; not account equity or a loss cap. Estimated primary round trip $0.04/share, plus assumed short borrow 3% annual /252 for one day; commission zero. Costs and borrow availability are assumptions, not observed fills. Lower gap = kept worse order minus removed better order; upper gap = kept better order minus removed worse order.

The hourly and four-hour 50 EMA pair did not earn its place here. This is the original groups’ recorded pooled comparison. Longs and shorts point opposite ways; a common side-mix calculation leaves FULL unresolved. It does not establish whether agreement adds information or improves future trades.

1. Scoped descriptive answer and source grant

The hourly and four-hour 50 EMAs are the specific pair. Of the 5,211 removed entries, 883 agree on another pair; those other pairs are outside this comparison. This is DESCRIPTIVE, with no future-money inference. [N:429; N:13]

Iliya Sivkov / Trading Fanatic teaches agreement as a confluence within a full system. We grant that distinction. Our study isolates one mechanical reading, with our exits and numeric slope rule. On indices, Iliya uses “a bit more of a VWAP” (471.12-479.919 seconds in the original tutorial).

Source video: How I Replaced Market Structure with One Line (Full Tutorial). Quoted words are supported by saved captions; caption start times are not verified word timing.

[MEASURED: method] The lower / upper pair, in plain words. Our data are one-minute bars. When one minute's bar touches both a trade's stop and its target, the bar cannot show which came first. "Lower" assumes the worse order for every such minute; "upper" assumes the better order. For the gap: lower = kept on the worse order minus removed on the better order; upper is the reverse . The pair is not a confidence interval and says nothing about luck . Ambiguous events at $0.04 : - FULL: 41 of 6,596 - EARLY: 9 of 1,428 - DEVELOPMENT: 18 of 4,120 - HELD-OUT: 14 of 1,048

[MEASURED] Why DEVELOPMENT (2012-2023) reads EXECUTION-ORDER UNRESOLVED. On the worse order, the kept trades trail by 0.0096 R; on the better order, they lead by 0.0173 R . The sign of the gap depends on an order the minute bars cannot show, so no direction is reported for these twelve years. That is the 2012-23 blank, shown on screen, not footnoted. Its kept and removed means are themselves almost equal: -0.1727 / -0.1587 against -0.176 / -0.1631 .

[INFERRED: arithmetic, from FR] The blank holds after our estimated costs, including the assumed short borrow . - Before costs, DEVELOPMENT's kept trades trailed on both price orders: gross contrast -0.041 / -0.0141. - With the spread but no borrow, they still trailed: -0.0463 / -0.0194. - The sign also moves when small stops are dropped: +0.0001 / +0.011 (KEPT-BETTER) without planned risks of $0.05 or less, and -0.0107 / -0.005 (KEPT-WORSE) without $0.10 or less.

EARLY shorts are better only after primary estimated costs and are price-order unresolved at the lower $0.02 cost. Borrow availability and expense are assumptions, not executable returns.

6. Locked-design summary and support/missing-data limits

Summary, not the full plan text

Locked before the completed run: a32-prereg-lock-2 (8c4c8f2). The first attempt stopped before a simulated trade; its record is preserved. The second run completed and wrote results; no saved receipt records its process exit code.

The lock commit is in a private repository without a public immutable ref. It identifies our saved plan; it is not public timestamp proof.

DESCRIPTIVE; no interval or luck inference

Amendment 1: the interval method failed calibration in 3 of 5 synthetic scenarios; the study became descriptive before market results.

Amendment 2: after the first run refused before a trade, one impossible minute was treated as missing, counted and never repaired; a second lock preceded the completed run.

[MEASURED: our specification] The entry is OUR reading of Iliya's lower-frame rule. Iliya says: "How does the break work? We need the body closure above or below the MA. That is our confirmation." . We read that as a 15-minute close crossing the 15-minute 50 EMA. A long needs the previous close at or below the previous EMA and the current close above the current EMA; a short is the mirror . The rest of the trade is also ours, not Iliya's : - Fill: the next minute's open. - Stop: one cent beyond the signal candle's extreme. - Target: two times the planned risk. - Time exit: at 120 minutes, or at the last minute's open. - Unit: R = result divided by the planned risk per share, fixed before entry. [MEASURED: our cost estimates] Round trip, per share: $0.02, $0.04 (primary) or $0.10. Shorts also pay an assumed 3% annual borrow for one day. Commission is 0 . These are estimates, not broker quotes. [MEASURED: comparison design] The entries are the same in both groups, with identical exits and costs. - KEPT: at the decision, the completed 1-hour and 4-hour 50 EMAs both point the trade's way: close on the trade's side of the EMA, and slope the trade's way . - REMOVED: every other entry, split into against / mixed / flat . The slope rule is a numeric one we chose . Iliya says: "There is no good slope. You just need to see it visually trending higher or lower." .

Retrospective complete regular sessions with 250 prior valid bars per frame. This is retrospective selection, not a real-time tradable support screen; no inference to excluded sessions.

[MEASURED] The tail . 96 of the 6,596 entries are below -2 R net on the lower path at $0.04. Their gross results on that path: - 5 positive (+1.0 to +2.0). All 5 are target exits that won before costs and still lost more than 2 R net on a tiny stop. - 3 exactly 0. - 88 negative. Only 1 is below -2 R gross: SPY 2020-03-16, -2.9032, ambiguous exit, planned risk $0.31.

Among the 96, exit reasons are 64 stop, 24 ambiguous, 5 target and 3 entry-gap. 72 of the 96 are shorts, and 79 have a planned risk of $0.05 or less.

[MEASURED] The worst trades . The six worst of the 6,596 are the five listed above in the worst-trades table plus SPY 2009-09-14 (-6.242). All six are shorts with a planned risk of $0.01 per share, so the $0.04 spread alone is 4 R. - The entry-gap mechanism. The two worst (SPY 2021-03-17 and SPY 2020-12-08) and the worst kept trade (QQQ 2020-03-16, -6.0417, also a $0.01 short) are the run's only 3 entry-gap exits. Each filled already beyond a barrier and closed at the fill price , so its gross result is exactly 0: the trade never moved. - The borrow share. SPY 2021-03-17's -8.6977 R is 4 R of estimated spread plus 4.6977 R of the assumed one-day borrow. SPY 2020-12-08's -8.3867 R is 4 R plus 4.3867 R.

These losses come from tiny stops, where fixed per-share costs are many times the planned risk. They are not market moves. They are kept, never trimmed .

7. Reopen evidence and downloads; respectful source credit

Reopen evidence: an exact source slide or slope rule under a new preregistration while preserving this result; a custodied EURUSD, GBPUSD and gold minute dataset; timestamped orders, fills and fees. None of these is a rerun authorized by this report.

The primary D00 ledger contains 6,596 saved simulated entries, 1,385 kept plus 5,211 removed, on our reading for SPY and QQQ; on indices, Iliya uses a bit more of a VWAP (471.12-479.919 seconds in the original tutorial). IWM, DIA and alternative-design rows are separate study outputs. Per-event net R is the exact cost-specific numerator divided by denominator. Prices and risk are stored in integer millionths per share; they are not portfolio values.

ColumnMeaning and unit

RASTER-01THE 50-EMA ON THE HIGHER TIMEFRAMES The General Guidelines: Trade in the Direction of the EMA. 4H Bullish Zone, price above the 4H EMA and EMA is sloping up. 1H Bullish zone, price below the 1H EMA and EMA is sloping down. Consider the Slope of the EMA. Inclined EMA Slope = Trending Market. Flat EMA = Consolidating Market. The EMA is a Dynamic Support/Resistance level. Look for Bounce plays from it. Never trade against it when it’s tapped. Wait for it to break and retest. You can only trade towards it, while it’s not tapped yet (counter-trend trade). Look for EMA Agreement across timeframes. If the EMA direction is the same on 2+ timeframes – you have a good bias.B01-s01; accepted-cut frame 0; 0.00000..0.04167 s; frames 0..0RASTER:iliya_agreement; ART:iliya_agreement; Literal source-image transcription; source wording, not our result. Download the film-figure index | Report-library summary

The film says: “We publish a free test report for each episode on our site, with numbers, written plans and what would change our answer; the back catalogue is still being filled in.” Written plans here means the written summary of the plan’s main terms, not full private plan text. Numbers are the saved tables, primary trade ledger and cut inventory; reopen evidence is stated in this section.

These downloads do not contain raw minute bars, the full plan text, synthetic qualification receipts, secondary-fund or alternative-design ledgers, or every diagnostic output. A source hash identifies a saved record; it does not make that private record downloadable. We are still filling in the back catalogue.

This research cannot answer whether the gap is luck, whether it persists, or how Iliya’s discretionary system, accounts or services perform.
